title: Artigo 10.º - Mais-valias
search_text: article_block art-cirs-10 https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/legislacao-consolidada/lei/2014-70048167-70051792 '10' act-cirs note-cirs-hpp-reinvestment # Artigo 10.º - Mais-valias Relevant HPP reinvestment rules from the current official text: - Gains from the sale of real rights over immovable property are capital gains. - Gains from selling a property used as the taxpayer's or household's own permanent home are excluded from taxation if the statutory reinvestment conditions are met. - The reinvestment base is the value of realization minus repayment of any loan originally used to acquire the sold property. - The reinvestment may be in: - acquisition of ownership of another property, - land for construction and/or respective construction, - enlargement or improvement of another property, - in all cases exclusively for the same purpose of own permanent home. - The replacement property may be in Portugal or in another EU/EEA state with tax information exchange. - Timing rule: reinvestment must occur between 24 months before and 36 months after the sale date. - The taxpayer must declare the intention to reinvest in the tax return for the year of sale, even if reinvestment is only partial. - The sold property must have been the taxpayer's or household's own permanent home, proven through tax domicile, in the 12 months before the sale, unless exceptional circumstances apply. - There is no benefit if: - on acquisition of another property, the acquirer does not assign it to own permanent home within 12 months after reinvestment, - in the other cases, registration/matrix requirements and later assignment deadlines are missed, - the taxpayer or household does not fix tax domicile in the replacement property, - specific anti-abuse/public-support cases in article 10(6)(d) apply. - If reinvestment is only partial, the exclusion only applies proportionally to the reinvested part.

title: Artigo 43.º - Mais-valias
search_text: article_block art-cirs-43 https://info.portaldasfinancas.gov.pt/pt/informacao_fiscal/codigos_tributarios/cirs_rep/Pages/irs43.aspx '43' act-cirs note-cirs-hpp-reinvestment # Artigo 43.º - Mais-valias Relevant rule for real-estate gains: - The taxable capital-gains income is the annual net balance of gains and losses. - For resident taxpayers, the positive or negative balance for real-estate transfers under article 10(1)(a) is, in the ordinary case, considered only in 50% of its amount. - There is an exception where 100% is considered in the specific public-support situation described in article 43(2)(a).

title: HPP reinvestment note
search_text: consolidation_note note-cirs-hpp-reinvestment https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/legislacao-consolidada/lei/2014-70048167-70051792 act-cirs art-cirs-10 art-cirs-43 # HPP reinvestment note Assumption: this note concerns a resident individual selling a property that qualifies as habitação própria e permanente under CIRS article 10. Current operative reading from the indexed slice: - On the sale of a personal home, the gain is ordinarily a category G real-estate capital gain under CIRS article 10. - In the ordinary resident case, only 50% of the net gain is considered for IRS under article 43. - That gain can be excluded from taxation, in whole or in part, if the legal reinvestment regime for own permanent home is satisfied. - The amount that matters for reinvestment is not the gross sale price. It is the value of realization after deducting repayment of any mortgage/loan originally taken to acquire the sold home. - Full exclusion requires full qualifying reinvestment of that net realization amount. Partial reinvestment leads only to proportional exclusion. - The reinvestment window is broad but strict: from 24 months before the sale to 36 months after the sale. - The taxpayer must state the intention to reinvest in the return for the year of sale. - The replacement property must also become the taxpayer's or household's own permanent home, with the timing conditions in article 10(6). - The sold property must itself have been the taxpayer's or household's own permanent home, normally evidenced by tax domicile in the 12 months before sale, subject to the exceptional-circumstances rule in article 10(23). This note is sufficient for scoped archive answers about the general HPP reinvestment rule, but it is not yet a full article-by-article personal-tax vertical for every edge case.
